description: Hand-written frozen answers for stream-level frame decode. Not a copy of any one arm: every case was ruled against the reconcile classes in notes/companion-app/shared-core/plan.md and then assembled from the arm that already implements the ruling. The base is rust-bridge, because resync-past-bad-magic is the ratified decoder (Class D); the corrupt-gzip case comes from the mobile arms, because both Rust decoders wedge there (Class A). An arm conforms when its frame-stream-trace.<impl>.json matches these constants and every step of every case, skipping the fields its unobserved array declares. No arm conforms on every case today; Phase 3 replaces all five with one WireEndec, and that is what has to satisfy this file.

reconciled.resync: RESYNC, SILENTLY. Class D, ratified: bad magic, an unsupported version and an over-cap length all scan forward for the next 0xdead and keep decoding, and the scan holds back the last magic-length-1 bytes so a magic split across a read is not lost. No error event is emitted, because the seam is a tokio_util Decoder and any Err from decode ends a Framed stream for good, so a decoder that reports a resync as an error cannot also survive it; resyncs are a tracing concern, not a stream event. rust-bridge conforms. rust-gateway clears the whole buffer and errors, destroying every frame already read into it. swift, kotlin and ts throw without consuming, so the accumulator re-reads the same bad header forever and the connection is dead in a different way. Cases: bad-magic-mid-stream-then-valid-frame, leading-garbage-then-valid-frame, magic-straddling-a-read-boundary-in-garbage, bad-magic-with-no-valid-frame-after, unsupported-version-then-valid-frame, length-just-over-the-rust-cap-then-valid-frame, length-two-to-the-sixty-third-then-valid-frame, length-u64-max-then-valid-frame.
reconciled.max_payload_bytes: 16777216. Class B, numeric, daemon wins: the daemon caps a declared payload at 16 MiB, the mobile accumulators at 8 MiB, and GatewayEndec has no cap at all. The cap is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it u64::MAX in the length field overflows the header-plus-payload sum and panics (rust-gateway does exactly that), and 2^63 parks the decoder on a wait that can never be satisfied. Under the ruling an over-cap length is a resync, so a declared 16 MiB + 1 recovers the frame behind it instead of killing the stream. A length between the two caps (12 MiB) is legal and the decoder simply waits for the bytes: terminal incomplete, no event.
reconciled.decompress_failure: RECOVER AND CONTINUE. Class A, both Rust arms are defective. Framing is intact when inflation fails - the body was consumed off the front of the buffer before the gzip reader ran - so the next frame is decodable, and swift, kotlin and ts all decode it. Both Rust decoders return the io error through `?` while the parse state still holds the dead frame header, so every later call compares fresh bytes against the dead frame total_length, returns Ok(None) and never decodes anything again. The state reset must happen before decompression, not after it, and the error must be classified recoverable, which today means splitting decompression out of EndecError::Io - `is_recoverable` currently answers false for it and that answer contradicts this ruling.
reconciled.unknown_compression_and_encoding: COERCE. Class C, adopted default, flagged for review: an unrecognised compression byte reads as none and an unrecognised encoding byte reads as msgpack, per BridgeEndec. Framing never depends on either byte, so the frame is still consumed exactly and the stream stays aligned; a payload that really was in an unknown format then fails typed decode as a recoverable error. The mobile accumulators instead throw without consuming, which stalls the stream on a byte that costs nothing to survive. The alternative worth Joey overruling this with: reject the frame but skip its body, which keeps the stream aligned AND preserves the signal that a peer spoke something we do not understand. Coercion silently misdecodes a future compression scheme; rejection loses the frame either way but says so.
reconciled.typed_decode_failure: RECOVER AND CONTINUE, recoverable true. Every arm already agrees: the body is consumed, the error is reported, the next frame decodes. Covered by zero-length-frame-then-valid-frame and valid-framing-invalid-payload-then-valid-frame.
reconciled.recoverable_field: Class E, API asymmetry, recorded not asserted today. Only the Rust arms have an is_recoverable notion; swift, kotlin and ts report null because their error types carry none, which the differ counts as a divergence and is not one. The values here are the ratified Rust semantics. The asymmetry dissolves in Phase 3 when all five seams become one Rust decoder, at which point every arm can answer and the field becomes assertable.
reconciled.compression_and_encoding_fields: Recorded from the wire, not from rust-bridge. A tokio_util Decoder yields only priority plus the typed message, so both Rust arms declare compression and encoding unobserved and emit null; swift, kotlin and ts read them off the header and agree with each other everywhere. This file records the true header values so it stays a complete description of the stream, and a conforming Rust arm keeps declaring them unobserved rather than growing an item type to satisfy a corpus. The two coerced frames (unknown-compression-byte, unknown-encoding-byte) are recorded as the coerced values none and msgpack, which is what the ruling says the decoder saw.
reconciled.auto_gzip_threshold_bytes: 16256, encoder-side, asserted by no case here. Swift and Kotlin auto-gzip a normal-priority payload over 16256 bytes when the caller did not pick a compression; Rust and ts never auto-gzip, so every gzip frame on the wire today came from a phone. Class C, adopted default is to keep the threshold when the unified core takes both encoder paths, because the phone-to-daemon direction carries the OTA and webapp-bundle payloads and that is the link with the bandwidth problem. Flagged rather than settled: it is an encoder question that a decode corpus cannot answer, and the number itself is unexplained by anything in the tree.

asymmetries.compression: not visible through a tokio_util Decoder; see reconciled.compression_and_encoding_fields
asymmetries.encoding: not visible through a tokio_util Decoder; see reconciled.compression_and_encoding_fields
